reviewer: Codex source review in R1 Phase 1
note: Cause reviews do not replace upstream risk labels and are not independent human ground truth. Contributing boundaries are recorded; no isolated rule-change experiment was performed.

cases.reason: guess is ABC; charAt(1) selects B, which fixes bar to bob. Both nested input and output constructors receive a constant-derived path. Two primary records are distinct read/write operations sharing an argument range, not a duplicate traversal finding.
The constant ABC.charAt(1) selects B and bar=bob before FileInputStream. Other tainted branches are unreachable for this fixed selector.
Inner helper returns a fixed string: (7*42)-86 is 208, so the >200 branch always wins. Taint in an argument does not establish taint in this helper return.
After adding safe,param,moresafe and removing index 0, index 1 is moresafe. Null input leaves alsosafe. Collection position reasoning is absent from the observed match.
Same safe list-index helper behavior as 01240. The nested constructors yield two primary read/write records but only one independent pathtraver reference case.
The same-file helper chooses fixed B via ABC.charAt(1), returns bob, and the subsequent SQL receives a fixed value. Scanner match does not establish evaluation of the helper body.

External header controls SQL passed to Connection.prepareCall; CallableStatement.executeQuery has no SQL argument. Current JDBC rule sinks are Statement.execute/executeQuery/executeUpdate with an explicit tainted SQL argument. Source is modeled, but this sink shape is outside it.

Header reaches echo shell payload in argList, then no-argument ProcessBuilder followed by command(argList) and start. Existing rule models tainted constructor arguments, not later command mutation; list propagation is an additional boundary.
Servlet cookies/getValue supply param; this source is absent from current source lists. Constant selector charAt(2) chooses C and keeps tainted bar before adding a shell payload to a command list.
Cookie value enters fileName and FileInputStream(new File(fileName)); cookie source is not modeled. A constant base concatenated with external text is not a containment guard.

ThingFactory/ThingInterface wrap the return flow across files. Both local Thing implementations preserve input. JDBCtemplate is a static helper field typed in DatabaseHelper; the caller lacks its declaration, affecting typed framework matching. These coexist; attribution is not isolated.

Cookie value passes through an identity inner helper into File(base,bar).exists. The current path capability models selected I/O sinks, not this metadata/exists signature. This is a benchmark coverage boundary, not a proposed automatic scope expansion.
